| [LIT-2333](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2333.md) v2 | Metamorphic Testing: A Review of Challenges and Opportunities | Tsong Yueh Chen, Fei-Ching Kuo, Huai Liu, Pak-Lok Poon, Dave Towey, T. H. Tse and Zhi Quan Zhou (2018), ACM Computing Surveys 51(1), article 4, DOI 10.1145/3143561. A review by the originators of metamorphic testing: where no practical oracle checks one output, a program is checked against metamorphic relations, necessary properties of the target algorithm across two or more related inputs and their outputs. It formalizes the relations, corrects four common misreadings, and is explicit that the method alleviates the oracle problem and "can never completely solve it", since the relations are necessary, not sufficient. Read for the exchange "luria experiment design", where A proposed such relations as the hidden scorer of a change to a record's schema; the reading supports that use with three limits ([NOTE-1717](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1717.md)). | Active — Read on 2026-11-12 ([NOTE-1717](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1717.md)) from the authors' manuscript on the University of Wollongong's Research Online repository, hosted on Figshare (https://ro.uow.edu.au/articles/journal_contribution/Metamorphic_Testing_A_Review_of_Challenges_and_Opportunities/27764520, file https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/50531136), a copy lawful under [ADR-074](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-074.md).
